name: Covington
seo_title: 5 Christmas Events for Kids in Covington, WA 2026
seo_desc: 5 Christmas events for kids in Covington, WA, 3 free: Covington Community Tree Lighting at Don Henning Roundabout and more.
lede: Covington keeps Christmas small and local: a community tree lighting at the Don Henning Roundabout, a candy class at City Hall and a lights out swim at the aquatic center.
celebrates: The City of Covington's big holiday night is its Community Tree Lighting at the Don Henning Roundabout beside the Fred Meyer parking lot on SE 272nd Street, with free crafts and activities, cocoa and coffee, carols and a visit from Santa Claus. City Parks and Recreation runs Christmas Candy Camp at City Hall, and the Covington Aquatic Center closes the year with its Hollydaze Swim, a lights out session with games and music.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Covington held its Community Tree Lighting on Saturday, December 6, from 4 to 6 pm at the Don Henning Roundabout and Fred Meyer parking lot, 16735 SE 272nd Street. The city clerk even posted a public notice that a quorum of the Covington Youth Council might attend the lighting, with a note that no city business would be discussed. For 2026 the city has marked the lighting with a new date and time, moving it from a Saturday afternoon to a Friday evening.
facts: Covington began as a railroad stop. Around 1900 the Northern Pacific Railroad needed a short line between Kanasket and Auburn, and it sent a surveyor named Richard Covington to map the route, now known as the Palmer Cutoff. The last station on that line took his name, and the area, earlier called Jenkins Prairie, took the name of the stop. Covington became a city on August 31, 1997, after a large majority of residents voted for incorporation.
trains: Trains gave Covington its name. The Northern Pacific's Palmer Cutoff, surveyed by Richard Covington and completed in 1900, ended at a Covington station with a 2,850 foot passing track, a section house and a 24 man bunkhouse. Today the closest passenger rail is Sounder commuter rail at Kent and Auburn stations, and Link light rail at Kent Des Moines Station. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs its Santa Train, and the Mt. Rainier Scenic Railroad in Elbe offers steam trains.

traditions: The city gathers at the Don Henning Roundabout for free crafts, cocoa, carols, Santa Claus and the lighting of the community tree.
The Covington Aquatic Center ends its year of themed swims with a lights out holiday session full of games and music.
City Parks and Recreation brings in The Traveling Chocolate Company to teach chocolate tempering and candy making at City Hall.
Once the city lights the tree at the Don Henning Roundabout, it marks the start of the season for families on SE 272nd Street.
kidfact: Covington is named after a man who drew maps for a railroad. Richard Covington surveyed a train line for the Northern Pacific around 1900, and the station at the end of it, and then the whole town, took his name.
faq: Where is the Covington tree lighting?

The City of Covington holds its Community Tree Lighting at the Don Henning Roundabout beside the Fred Meyer parking lot, 16735 SE 272nd Street, Covington, WA 98042. The city lists free crafts and activities, cocoa and coffee, carols and a chance to meet Santa Claus before the community tree is lit.
Is the Covington Hollydaze Swim good for little kids?

Yes, with a parent in the pool. The Covington Aquatic Center is an indoor pool, and the city says children under six need a parent in the water within arm's reach at all times. Swimmers arrive 15 minutes early for a swim test, and the city recommends registering ahead on its ActiveNet site.
How did Covington get its name?

From the railroad. Around 1900 the Northern Pacific sent surveyor Richard Covington to lay out a short line from Kanasket to Auburn, now called the Palmer Cutoff. The last station was named Covington, and the area, earlier known as Jenkins Prairie, took the station's name. The city incorporated on August 31, 1997.
What is the nearest train station to Covington?

Covington has no passenger station today. The closest are the Sounder commuter rail stations in Kent and Auburn and the Link light rail station at Kent Des Moines, which opened in December 2025. For a Christmas train ride, families drive to the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie for its Santa Train.
What is Christmas Candy Camp in Covington?

It is a City of Covington Parks and Recreation class taught by The Traveling Chocolate Company in the Covington Community Room at City Hall, 16720 SE 271st Street. Students learn to melt and temper chocolate, then dip, cluster and decorate their own candies. The city lists an age range of 6 to 99, so parents can register alongside their kids.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Covington for 2026, and here is what he found: 5 family events, 3 of them free. The magic runs from December 4 (Covington Community Tree Lighting at Don Henning Roundabout) through December 19, with Covington Community Tree Lighting at Don Henning Roundabout (December 4), Christmas Candy Camp at Covington City Hall (December 12) and Hollydaze Lights Out Swim at Covington Aquatic Center (December 19) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website or an official city calendar, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Washington Christmas events for kids guide.
